q: Which cell organelle is responsible for the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids for secretion?
solution: The Golgi Apparatus (or Golgi body) functions as a factory in which proteins received from the ER are further processed and sorted for transport to their eventual destinations.

q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Bihar to complete a full five-year term?
solution: Shri Krishna Singh was the first Chief Minister of Bihar and the first to complete a full five-year term in office.

q: The "Phillips Curve" in economics represents the inverse relationship between:
solution: The Phillips Curve is an economic concept stating that inflation and unemployment have a stable and inverse relationship.

q: In computer systems, what is the purpose of the 'BIOS'?
options: To perform hardware initialization during the booting process
To protect the system from viruses
solution: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware used to perform hardware initialization during the booting process (power-on startup)

q: The "Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary" is located in which district of Bihar?
solution: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is located in the Bhagalpur district of Bihar, India

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament?
solution: Article 123 of the Constitution of India grants the President certain law-making powers to promulgate Ordinances when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session

q: "Aspirin" is the common name for which chemical compound?
solution: Aspirin, also known as acetylsalicylic acid, is a medication used to reduce pain, fever, or inflammation.

q: The "Tehri Dam", the highest dam in India, is constructed on which river?
solution: The Tehri Dam is the highest dam in India and is constructed on the Bhagirathi River in Uttarakhand.

q: Which among the following is a "Vestigial Organ" in the human body?
solution: A vestigial organ is an anatomical feature or behavior that no longer seems to have a purpose in the current form of an organism; the vermiform appendix is a classic example in humans

q: Who was the leader of the "Wahabi Movement" in Bihar?
solution: In Bihar, the Wahabi movement was led by Wilayat Ali and Enayat Ali of Patna.

q: The phenomenon of "Total Internal Reflection" is the principle behind the working of:
solution: Total Internal Reflection (TIR) is the basic principle used in the transmission of light signals through optical fibers.

q: What is the keyboard shortcut to "Lock" your Windows PC?
solution: Pressing the Windows Logo key + L on the keyboard locks the computer screen immediately.

q: The "Barabar Caves", the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, are located in which district of Bihar?
solution: The Barabar Hill Caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating from the Maurya Empire, located in the Jehanabad district of Bihar.

q: Which Mughal ruler built the "Buland Darwaza" to commemorate his victory over Gujarat?
solution: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri in 1601 to commemorate his victory over Gujarat.

q: The "Veblen Effect" in economics refers to goods for which demand increases as:
solution: The Veblen effect occurs when the demand for a luxury good increases as the price increases, because the higher price makes the good more desirable as a status symbol.

q: In the human ear, which part converts sound vibrations into electrical signals?
solution: The cochlea is a fluid-filled, spiral-shaped cavity in the inner ear that plays a vital role in hearing by converting sound vibrations into nerve impulses.

q: Which schedule of the Constitution deals with the "Anti-Defection Law"?
solution: The 10th Schedule of the Indian Constitution, popularly known as the Anti-Defection Act, was inserted by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985

q: What is the full form of 'JPEG' in image file formats?
solution: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, which is the name of the committee that created the standard.

q: Which river is known as the "Rishi-Kanya" and flows through the Amarkantak plateau?
solution: The Narmada River, also known as the Reva and previously also known as Rishi-Kanya, rises from the Amarkantak Plateau.

q: "Gresham's Law" in economics states that:
options: Good money drives out bad money
Bad money drives out good money
solution: Gresham's law is a monetary principle stating that "bad money drives out good".

q: The "Swaraj Party" was formed in 1923 by Motilal Nehru and whom?
solution: The Swaraj Party was established in January 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

q: Which gas is known as "Laughing Gas"?
solution: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O), commonly known as laughing gas, is used in surgery and dentistry for its anesthetic and analgesic effects.

q: During "Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer" (Cloning), the nucleus is removed from which type of cell?
solution: In SCNT, the nucleus of a somatic cell is transferred to the cytoplasm of an enucleated egg cell (an egg cell that has had its own nucleus removed).

q: Which constitutional body audits the accounts of the Union and State governments?
solution: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is the constitutional authority responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the state governments.

q: Which type of network topology connects all nodes to a single central cable?
solution: In a bus topology, all nodes are connected to a single central cable, called the bus or backbone.

q: What is the rank of Bihar in India in terms of "Population Density" as per the 2011 Census?
solution: As per the 2011 Census, Bihar has the highest population density among Indian states.

q: The "Human Development Index" (HDI) is published by which organization?
solution: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a statistical composite index of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators, published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

q: "Cache Memory" acts as a high-speed buffer between:
solution: Cache memory is a small, high-speed memory area that stores frequently used data to speed up the process of accessing it by the CPU, acting as a buffer between the CPU and main memory (RAM).

q: The "Cabinet Mission" came to India in which year?
solution: The Cabinet Mission came to India in March 1946 to discuss the transfer of power from the British government to Indian leadership

q: "Malachite" is an ore of which metal?
solution: Malachite is a green copper carbonate hydroxide mineral and an important ore of copper

q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the "Annual Financial Statement" (Budget)?
solution: According to Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, the President shall in respect of every financial year cause to be laid before both the Houses of Parliament the "annual financial statement".

q: "Galvanization" is the process of coating iron with which metal to prevent rusting?
solution: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron to prevent rusting.

q: Which Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during the reign of Ashoka?
solution: The Third Buddhist Council was convened in about 250 BCE at Pataliputra under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka

q: What is the full form of 'WORM' in computer storage?
solution: WORM stands for "Write Once, Read Many," a data storage technology that allows information to be written to a storage medium once and prevents the drive from erasing or modifying that data.

q: The "Panchayati Raj" system was first adopted by which state?
solution: The Panchayati Raj system was first inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on 2nd October 1959 in Nagaur district, Rajasthan

q: The "Blue Revolution" in India is related to the growth of which sector?
solution: The Blue Revolution refers to the time of intense growth in the worldwide aquaculture industry, specifically fish production.

q: Which instrument is used to measure "Atmospheric Pressure"?
solution: A barometer is a scientific instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure

q: In a database, "Data Integrity" refers to:
options: The accuracy and consistency of data
The number of tables in the database
solution: Data integrity is the maintenance of, and the assurance of, data accuracy and consistency over its entire life-cycle.

q: Which dam is built on the river Son in Bihar?
solution: The Indrapuri Barrage is built across the Son River in Rohtas district, Bihar.

q: The "Repo Rate" is the rate at which:
options: Commercial banks lend to the RBI
The RBI lends to commercial banks
Commercial banks lend to the public
The government borrows from the RBI
solution: Repo rate is the rate at which the central bank of a country (RBI in India) lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.

q: "Scurvy" is a disease caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
solution: Scurvy is a disease resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

q: Which key is used to "Indent" a paragraph in MS Word?
solution: In MS Word, the Tab key is commonly used to indent the first line of a paragraph.

q: The "Sher Shah Suri Tomb" is located in which city?
solution: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is in the Sasaram town of Bihar state.

q: "Engel's Law" states that as family income rises, the proportion of income spent on food:
solution: Engel's law is an economic observation stating that as income rises, the proportion of income spent on food falls, even if actual expenditure on food rises.

q: Which protocol is used for "Remote Login" to a computer over a network?
solution: Telnet is a network protocol used on the Internet or local area network to provide a bidirectional interactive text-oriented communication facility using a virtual terminal connection

q: The "Kaimur Plateau" is famous for which of the following?
solution: The Kaimur Plateau in Bihar is famous for its limestone deposits.

q: What is the chemical formula for "Washing Soda"?
solution: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, with the chemical formula .

q: Which pass connects Srinagar and Leh?
solution: Zoji La is a high mountain pass in the Himalayas at the boundary between the Ladakh and Kashmir valleys, connecting Srinagar to Leh.

q: The "Maximum Gap" between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed:
solution: According to the Constitution of India, the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot be more than six months.

q: "Ransomware" is a type of malware that:
solution: Ransomware is a type of malicious software designed to block access to a computer system or encrypt files until a sum of money is paid

q: The first session of the Bihar Provincial Congress was held in 1908 at:
solution: The first session of the Bihar Provincial Congress was held at Patna in 1908

q: Which device converts "Chemical Energy" into "Electrical Energy"?
solution: A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy through electrochemical reactions

q: Who was the first Mughal Emperor to have a "Coronation" in Patna?
solution: Farrukhsiyar was the first Mughal emperor to be crowned in Patna in 1713.

q: "Aqua Regia" is a mixture of which two acids?
solution: Aqua regia is a mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid, optimally in a molar ratio of 1:3.

q: In MS Excel, the intersection of a row and a column is called a:
solution: In a spreadsheet, a cell is the intersection between a row and a column.

q: Which Fundamental Right was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the "Heart and Soul of the Constitution"?
solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the "Heart and Soul of the Constitution" because it provides a remedy for the violation of fundamental rights.

q: What is the "Time Limit" for the government to provide information under the RTI Act, 2005 (general cases)?
solution: Under the RTI Act, 2005, a Public Information Officer (PIO) must provide information within 30 days of receiving the application.

q: "Mycology" is the study of:
solution: Mycology is the branch of biology concerned with the study of fungi.

q: The "Gandak River" joins the Ganga near which place?
solution: The Gandak River joins the Ganga at Sonepur, which is near Patna.

q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for "Routing" data packets?
solution: The Network Layer is the third layer of the OSI model and is responsible for packet forwarding and routing.

q: "Kunwar Singh" led the Revolt of 1857 from which place in Bihar?
solution: Kunwar Singh was a notable leader during the Indian Rebellion of 1857, leading the revolt from Jagdishpur.

q: What is the SI unit of "Luminous Intensity"?
solution: The candela (symbol: cd) is the SI unit of luminous intensity.

q: Which part of the cell is known as the "Suicide Bag"?
solution: Lysosomes are known as the suicide bags of the cell because they contain digestive enzymes; if the cell gets damaged, the lysosome may burst and digest its own cell.

q: The "Simla Pact" (1972) was signed between Indira Gandhi and:
solution: The Simla Agreement was signed between Indira Gandhi, the Prime Minister of India, and Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto, the President of Pakistan, on 2 July 1972.

q: Which function key is used to "Edit" the content of a cell in MS Excel?
solution: In MS Excel, pressing the F2 key allows you to edit the active cell.
